tagging.  Before sales pitch :    Try it out multiple times, hide the weak
areas During the pitch    As you said, divert is best option. Hiding or making

testing' kind of responses - shows your fire fighting skills  -making it an
opportunity to prove yourself - how you handle - will be a testimony. After
the pitch :   If it's a crucial one, get back when it works. Two more
additional insights :    When Jobs released his first iphone, they hard coded
signal strength as the phone cudn't catch the signal.   The battery is so
pathetic that a full charge works only for a single feature demo - Jobs took
multiple phones to demonstrate it and no one even knew why he did so. They
thought it was 'cool . As a startup, we don't have luxury of evaluating
clients and rejecting them. But in B2B, it's really important to NOT work with
that 20% clients who aren't productive. So, a reaction of your client during
such vulnerable situation gives a lot of inputs about what they are. So, in
case you are in a position to ignore, leave them
